rounds.text: Auro Impex & Chemicals Ltd suffers from a severe, accelerating deceleration in top-line growth that invalidates its headline valuation multiples, as compounded sales growth has turned negative at -7% over 3 years and -11% over the trailing twelve months [E13, E14]. This contraction is underscored by a sharp year-over-year sales decline of 21% [E62]. Furthermore, the company's profitability generation is structurally deteriorating across multiple timeframes, with the median return on equity collapsing from a 5-year median of 18% down to a 3-year median of 13% and sinking further to a low 9% over the last year [E20, E21, E22, E55]. Compounding these fundamental headwinds, the stock sits at a mere 12% of its 52-week range—languishing near its lows of ₹ 21 against a high of ₹ 58—and offers zero dividend yield to compensate shareholders for holding a lagging asset [E4, E5]. Conceded: the company trades at a low price-to-book ratio of 0.69x against a book value of ₹ 37.2 and exhibits a single-digit P/E ratio [E1, E2].
